title: 4541007B-Need_for_Speed_Most_Wanted.xiso.iso
queue_order: Queued by the lane (an env A/B on one binary; arms.sh skips a_ref == b_ref, so this is not left for the automatic arms job): four requests of one run each, OFF, ON, ON, OFF (request.sh --who fastpaths1010 --title 4541007B-Need_for_Speed_Most_Wanted.xiso.iso --route nfs-mw-quickrace --seconds 500 --perflog --device nova --ref 1ca4a6bd12 [--env <each of a_env> for OFF, no --env for ON] --issue 433 --expect this file), HAKUX_RELEASE_PRIO=1. ON queues with no --env: the app's own 'Fast renderer paths' switch (default on) sets all six vars from MainActivity, so the request proves the SHIPPED default, not a hand-set env. OFF's --env overrides the switch back to each var's C default (off), applied after MainActivity by xemu_android.cpp. The pilot gate (30 min of device time) is covered in two batches of two: OFF+ON first, pilots/fastpaths1010.ok written from their read, then ON+OFF.
baseline: No run of this exact six-switch-together binary exists yet. Nearest OFF readings, all plain (no --perflog) unless noted: texscan1010-nfs.json's off arm, warm countdown 46.4-46.6 ms (1-1791648919-texscan1010-2004607, perflog) and 41.9-43.5 ms (perdrawon1010's two off runs, no fastpaths/drawrec/reportasync); drawrec1010's probe base arm (all six on, ref bf43e8c4ef) read warm countdown 34.1-34.3 ms with its own proberead.py; postput1010-nfs.json's A arm (REPORT_ASYNC+TEXSCAN only, ref c63ec9774f) read warm 33.5-34.0 ms. The brief's own figure for all six on: 'about 33.7 ms (postput1010 arm A2, 77% of frames at v2)', from the postput1010 lane's own reading of the all-six base, not yet folded to this branch's predictions directory.
prediction: #433 the app's default 'Fast renderer paths' switch (all six vars on, set from MainActivity, no --env) against the switches' own C default (all six off, forced by --env) at the NFS MW race start, same binary. This is the combination postput1010, drawrec1010, texscan1010 and perdrawon1010 each measured separately or in smaller combinations; the switch adds no new mechanism, so ON should read close to drawrec1010's and postput1010's own all-six-on figures (~33.7-34.3 ms warm) and OFF should read in the band every plain (no switches) run of this route has shown (41.9-46.6 ms warm, texscan1010/perdrawon1010 baselines). Point estimate: ON warm countdown 34.0 ms (+-0.5), OFF warm countdown 44.0 ms (+-3.0, the off band is wide run to run). W: ON <= 36.0 ms -- generous against the 33.7-34.3 ms band already on record, so a fail would mean this exact binary (the switch's own code path, not a hand --env) does not reach what the component lanes measured. D: OFF - ON >= 5.0 ms -- the component lanes' gap is 8-12 ms; 5.0 ms is a loose floor that only a largely-inert toggle (env not reaching native, or a build that silently rebuilt with different defaults) would miss. What refutes it: W passes, D fails -- OFF is not actually running with the switches off (an env_vars ordering regression, or the build caching an old binary); D passes, W fails -- the toggle reaches native but this binary's ON is slower than every component lane's figure (a regression introduced by having all six wired through one path, or a device/thermal difference this session's baselines do not share, since none of the baselines above are from the same session as this run).
expect_note: Named rules read by docs/lanes/fastpaths1010/fpread.py --expect (legs V, W, D, in that order); a soak writes no captures. V also requires an s*-g11 frame for every valid warm start with a moving car, checked by eye and recorded in NOTES.md.
